coverage_note: 00:00-06:00 English only (app demo). Homework review 06:10-12:12, then busbut/binbisit drill to 21:00, then zaajj/anza3aj drill to end. Many Medi Arabic lines are Latin-transliterated (enbistee, basatatni, az'ajtu, ma tiz'ajni, matanzajini, banzaj...). Engine mishears: 08:57/08:59 Amal 'سعود' = صوّروا (echo of his word); 16:21 Amal 'انبسطتني' = بسطتني; 31:06/31:18/31:50 Amal 'أزعجتُ' = أزعجتوه (she is saying the -oh ending); 43:07/43:29 Amal 'سيفاء' = عاصفة; 44:24 Amal 'أنا مضايقة' = يلا المضارع; 1:02:14 Medi 'تعال' = probably تمام/سلام at goodbye. echo-candidates checked: 03:07 'Yeah, it's...' real English; 06:31 'Like,' real English; 10:34 'Kulil' = كل الـ (he started كل الناس); 35:08 'biz-' = start of بيزعجني; 36:30 'Ma tiz,' = ما تز(عجني); 42:33 'Yeah, either.' real English; 45:49 'say?' real English (I also say?); 48:58 'Huh?' real English; 49:29 'Oh,' real English; 50:47 / 51:23 'Matanzajini' = his ما تنزعجيني (filed as B12 row 0905-25). Pronunciation only, not filed: 25:44 'el swat' dropped hamza (filed low as A9 in case it is the plural); 33:44 'biniz'aj' vowel (Amal: ej sound, F2); 36:42 'ما تعزجيني' ز/ع root-letter swap (S4); 48:08 'تزعن' (S4); 55:16 Amal heard 'hot' (شوب) in his شبعان, engine wrote شبعان both times, dropped ع = S4; 34:54 'hadha al-jaw' MSA pronunciation. Not slips: 25:27 maz'ooj -> maz'ooja self-fix; 38:38 مزو -> مزعج self-fix; 41:17 انزعج -> انزعجت self-fix; 44:28 بزعج -> بنزعج self-fix; 58:22 أتعبك -> أتعبها self-fix; 59:18 باتعبها -> أتعبها self-fix; 42:28 انزعجتي / انزعجتِ Amal said both fine; 39:37 بيزعجوني repeat of 38:50 (one row); 51:40 Azajitini built right. Chat: no CHAT lines in this transcript (Amal typed بزعج / مزعج in Meet chat around 21:42-22:46 but the chat is not in the file).

rows.medi_said: Okay, so isn't it en-enbistee? Did you enjoy? ... I put enbustee.
rows.amal_said: "انبسطتي." ... I guess in the past ... Yes, it is double T.
rows.why: Past 'you (f) enjoyed' needs the -ti ending on the past stem (انبسط + تي = انبسطتي); he dropped the past-tense t (enbistee = انبستي) and said at 07:03 he thought the t was removed; Amal recast انبسطتي and confirmed 'it is double T'; he admits 'I just forgot the double T'.
rows.english: Did you enjoy your time outside?

rows.medi_said: Did you enjoy, past tense, your time outside? Okay, so isn't it en-enbistee?
rows.amal_said: what is it-- what is missing? It's not "انبسطتي." Something is missing. What is it? ... "في" or be?
rows.why: انبسط takes في / بـ before the thing enjoyed (sheet: 'have fun / enjoy | Enbese6 (fi | انبسط'); his homework sentence had no preposition, Amal prompted 'what is missing?' and he found it: 'The في, I totally forgot', then 07:56 انبسطتي في وقتك.
rows.english: Did you enjoy your time outside?

rows.medi_said: Yeah, انبسط didn't I? ... It makes someone... You're right, you're right. So this is without the B.
rows.amal_said: You put "انبسط". ... Does the تخييم have emotions? Does it get happy? It makes everyone happy.
rows.why: 'Camping made everyone happy' is make-happy (بسط), not get-happy (انبسط); Amal pointed at 'you put انبسط' and asked whether camping has emotions until he fixed it to التخييم بسط at 10:10.
rows.english: Camping made everyone happy and excited.

rows.medi_said: التخييم بسط كل حدا و حَمَس
rows.amal_said: Let's put the verbs together. ... بسط وحمس
rows.why: He split the two verbs around the object (made everyone happy and excited); Amal told him to put the verbs together first (بسط وحمس) and then the object, an Arabic word-order fix.
rows.english: Camping made everyone happy and excited.

rows.medi_said: كل حدا ... كل الناس؟
rows.amal_said: كل حدا or what's everyone? ... الكل.
rows.why: For 'everyone' he said كل حدا then كل الناس; Amal prompted 'what's everyone?' and supplied her sheet word (sheet: 'everybody / all / everyone | El-kul | الكل').

rows.medi_said: Is it, isn't it lisa ma bansabit? ... so ma mis-- Ma lisa ma en-enbisit.
rows.amal_said: This is I don't get happy yet. What about don't get happy? It's a command. ... Command, so we keep the... ... ما تنبسط لسه.
rows.why: 'Don't get happy yet' is a negative command (ما + you-form: ما تنبسط), he gave the negated present 'I don't get happy' (ما بنبسط); Amal said 'It's a command' and prompted until he produced ما تنبسط at 11:47.

rows.medi_said: Ma teenbesit lisa ma ba'arif kul shey.
rows.amal_said: Ma, we don't know.
rows.why: The homework sentence was 'we don't know everything'; he said ma ba'arif (I don't know) and Amal prompted 'we don't know' until he said ma ben a'arif (ما بنعرف) at 12:01.
rows.english: Don't get happy yet, we don't know everything.

rows.medi_said: Imbare lele or lele imbare.
rows.amal_said: ليلة امبارح.
rows.why: Amal asked how to say 'last night' ('I don't think we've ever used it'); he offered both orders, she supplied ليلة امبارح and he said 'That's a new word we need to add' - a didn't-know, not a slip (he asked X or Y).

rows.medi_said: Um انبسط، انبسط حفلة... حفلتك.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. We forgot something. ... في
rows.why: انبسط takes في / بـ before the thing enjoyed; he dropped it again, Amal said 'Mm-mm, we forgot something' and he fixed to انبسطي في حفلتك at 18:51-18:59.

rows.medi_said: Okay. So ma'tanbisti halak. ... بفي حالك ... في حالك
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I'm gonna keep making you repeat until you say في on your own. ... ما تنبسط بحالك. That's في or ب.
rows.why: Third time the في / بـ after انبسط is missing ('don't enjoy yourself'); Amal said Mm-mm and that she will keep making him repeat until he says في on his own; he then added في حالك.

rows.medi_said: Fi halak. And I don't know how to say too much, right?
rows.amal_said: You can say كتير. كتير or extra.
rows.why: He said he does not know 'too much' and Amal supplied كتير (sheet: 'a lot / very / much | Kteer | كتير') - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: زيادي
rows.amal_said: زيادة.
rows.why: For 'extra' he said زيادي twice (20:18 and 20:22); Amal recast زيادة and he repeated it (sheet: 'extra / increase | Ziaadeh | زيادة') - wrong form of a word he knows.

rows.medi_said: so انبسطي ب ليلك
rows.amal_said: This your night. One night. ... بليلتك. Yes.
rows.why: ليلة (one night, feminine) grows a -t before the owner ending: ليلتك; he said ليلك (lail + ak, as if from ليل), Amal prompted 'one night' and he fixed to ليلتك at 20:49, she confirmed بليلتك.

rows.medi_said: so I, I think I remembered mazuj as annoying ... and مزعـ مزعج as annoyed.
rows.amal_said: بالعكس. ... If it has this oo sound. مزعوج، موجوع، محروج، مجروح. All of them is annoyed. Feeling the thing, not causing it.
rows.why: He swapped the two words (sheet: 'annoyed | Maz3ooj | مزعوج', 'annoying | Muz3ej | مزعج'); Amal said بالعكس (the opposite) and gave the -oo- = feeling rule; at 22:24-22:46 he could not produce مزعج either (mazuj / mozuj) until he read it in the chat.

rows.medi_said: متعب؟ ... Mmm, No.
rows.amal_said: Do you remember متعب؟ ... is tiring. ... Same pattern as مزعج.
rows.why: Amal asked if he remembers متعب (tiring); he said No and she supplied the meaning - a didn't-know, not a slip (not on her sheet as an adjective; 'tired | Ta3baan' and 'i cause tiredness | Ana bata33eb' are).

rows.medi_said: These voices or sounds are annoying. "hadhol el swat."
rows.amal_said: الأصوات.
rows.why: Plural of صوت is أصوات (broken plural); he said 'el swat' and Amal recast الأصوات - may only be the dropped initial hamza (pronunciation, S4), filed low so the third reader can rule.

rows.medi_said: هي زعجت زعجتك
rows.amal_said: أزعجتك. See? It's easier to say أزعجتك.
rows.why: Amal had just asked for the a- form (أزعج, 'more used than زعج'); he said زعجتك, she recast أزعجتك and he said 'Oh, that's right, أزعجتك' - low because at 28:13 and 28:56 she said both forms are valid and 'you should learn both' (both-forms-fine rule).

rows.medi_said: Az'aj, az'ajtu. ... Uh, أزعجتو... ... if it's az'ajtu and az'ajtu.
rows.amal_said: أزعجتُ. You can't say أزعجتُ، wo. ... Doesn't sound right. ... Yes, there is an h.
rows.why: 'You guys annoyed him' needs the object -h on the verb (أزعجتوا + ه = أزعجتوه); he stopped at az'ajtu (you-pl annoyed) with no 'him', Amal said you can't say that and confirmed the -h ending when he asked (engine wrote her أزعجتوه as 'أزعجتُ').

rows.medi_said: don't want to annoy them. Ana ma, ma bitti, az'ajkum.
rows.amal_said: أزعجهم.
rows.why: 'them' is the -hum ending; he put -kum (you pl) on the verb, Amal recast أزعجهم and he repeated it.
rows.english: I don't want to annoy them.

rows.medi_said: So الولاد أزعجوا، أزعجوا
rows.amal_said: أزعجوه؟
rows.why: 'Did the kids annoy him' needs the object -h on the verb; he stopped at أزعجوا (they annoyed) with no 'him', Amal recast أزعجوه and he repeated it - second time this lesson (see 30:53).

rows.medi_said: هو بيزعج، بيزعجوني.
rows.amal_said: بيزعج، ... بيزعجني.
rows.why: Subject is هو (he) so the verb is بيزعج + ني = بيزعجني; he used the they-form بيزعجوني, Amal prompted 'بيزعج،' and he fixed to بيزعجني; he repeated the same slip at 39:37 (Amal recast بزعجني, he: 'Why did I have the oo in there?') - one row, the first.

rows.medi_said: إنت بتنزعج. إنتي بتنزعجي. إنتو بتنزعجو. هو بينزعج. هي بتنزعج. هما بينزعجو. إحنا بنن-بننزعج.
rows.amal_said: بننزعج. ... Been catching you saying the instead of the ب. ... ننزعج.
rows.why: Amal voiced 'Been catching you saying the [?] instead of the ب' and re-said ننزعج / بننزعج - the engine lost the sound she heard in place of the b- prefix (likely m- / mn-), so the slip is real but its exact shape is not in the transcript; filed low for the third reader.

rows.medi_said: ليش، ليش فرق من-- ليش فرق من WhatsApp? ... Why is it different than WhatsApp? ليش فرق؟
rows.amal_said: كيف؟ ... No because I'm using لأنه عم بستعمل الـ telephone.
rows.why: He used the noun فرق (a difference) as the adjective 'different' and من for 'than' (عن); Amal did not understand (كيف؟), he explained in English and she answered without fixing it - best reading: ليش مختلف عن / ليش غير, let pass.
rows.english: Why is it different than WhatsApp?

rows.medi_said: ما تنزعج، ما...
rows.amal_said: تنزعج. ما تنزعجي. احكيها كمان مرة.
rows.why: The negative command to Amal (f) is ما تنزعجي; he gave the masculine ما تنزعج, she recast the feminine and made him repeat it (48:08-48:39) - medium because at 50:18 she also uses ما تنزعج مني herself.

rows.medi_said: It does have an N. ma-matan, matanzajini.
rows.amal_said: No. ... By me. ما تنزعجي. ... Yes. ما تنزعجي مني.
rows.why: 'Don't get annoyed by me': انزعج is get-annoyed and takes من + person (مني), it cannot carry the object -ni on the verb; he said matanzajini (ما تنزعجيني), Amal said No and gave 'By me. ما تنزعجي ... مني', he then said matanzaji minni at 49:44.

rows.medi_said: Matanzajini. I think I just need to slow it down. Matanzajini.
rows.amal_said: Yes. ما تزعجني. ما تنزعج مني. احكيهم التنتين. ... It is there، but it's not ما تنزعجني. It's just ما تزعجني.
rows.why: 'Don't annoy me' is the make-X form ما تزعجيني (no n-); after her ما تزعجني at 50:07 he kept saying matanzajini (the get-X n- form + me) at 50:10, 50:47, 50:55, 51:13, 51:18, 51:23, 51:28, and Amal kept recasting ما تزعجني / ما تزعجيني ('it's not ما تنزعجني, it's just ما تزعجني') until he said ما تزعجيني at 51:32 - one row, the first after her fix; she also framed it as not stressing the عين, so part may be pronunciation.

rows.medi_said: So ana... Ana, so I get annoyed. It's present tense. Anabazaj. Na ba-banj.
rows.amal_said: Gets.
rows.why: 'I get annoyed' is the n- form بنزعج; he said ana bazaj (I annoy), Amal prompted 'Gets.' and he fixed to أنا بنزعج at 53:16 (sheet: 'i get annoyed | Banz3ej | بنزعج').

rows.medi_said: Yeah, أنا بنزعج، أ... لمّا...
rows.amal_said: If.
rows.why: The sentence was 'I get annoyed IF I'm hungry'; he reached for لما (when), Amal prompted 'If.' and he fixed: 'Oh, if. إذا'.
rows.english: I get annoyed if I'm hungry.

rows.medi_said: Oh, if. إذا، إذا أكون جوعان
rows.amal_said: بس إذا بكون، مش أكون. ليش؟ ... If is conditional، but it doesn't take out the be. It keeps it.
rows.why: iza keeps the b- on the next verb (إذا بكون); he dropped it (أكون), Amal said 'إذا بكون، مش أكون' and named the rule; he then said iza bakoon joan at 54:10.

rows.medi_said: أنا بزعج مين
rows.amal_said: mean or what's the better one؟ The one who. يلي.
rows.why: 'I annoy (the one) who annoys me' needs the relative اللي, not the question word مين; Amal asked for the better one ('The one who') and he said اللي at 56:27.

rows.medi_said: اللي who annoys me. Okay. So، اه، بينزعجني.
rows.amal_said: ليش أن annoys me.
rows.why: 'annoys me' is the make-X form بيزعجني; he used the get-X n- form بينزعجني, Amal asked 'ليش ن؟ annoys me' and he fixed: 'Oh, that's right, بيزعجني'.

rows.medi_said: اه، أنا، اه، زعلان. ... زعلان، زعلان.
rows.amal_said: زعلت. ... Here's your internal flip. ... زعلت. ... أنا ما انزعجت، أنا زعلت.
rows.why: His sentence was past ('I wasn't annoyed, I was sad'): أنا زعلان is present 'I am sad' with no was; Amal recast the past verb زعلت three times until he repeated it (كنت زعلان would also be past; she chose the verb to match ما انزعجت).
rows.english: I wasn't annoyed, I was sad.
